report.summary: Chunk 4 of typegraph.py: pass 2 resolution, edge emission, structural matching, hub capping, and coverage reporting.
risks: emit function | medium | The comment says 'An Enum member is a VALUE, not a typed field: parse.py forces its annotation to "" precisely so no member->type edge can be fabricated for it, and ``emit`` will count it as missing.' This claim is uncheckable because the chunk does not include the parse.py logic; we cannot verify that annotation is forced to "" for Enum members.

structural matching | medium | The comment says 'structural (Protocol) matching: a FLAGGED heuristic'. The heuristic uses `_member_names` and checks `wanted <= members[node_id]`. The correctness depends on `_member_names` implementation outside this chunk; uncheckable.

hub capping | medium | The comment says 'hub cap (I6): measured, applied, and published'. The code suppresses edges for targets exceeding `hub_cap` but the variable `hub_cap` is not defined in this chunk; uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Second pass: resolve annotations, emit edges for all relations, perform structural protocol matching, apply hub cap, and compute coverage statistics.

symbols.name: record
symbols.note: Records outcome kind and samples unresolved/ambiguous annotations.

symbols.name: emit
symbols.note: Resolves one annotation slot, updates site_counts, and appends edges to the edges dict if resolved.

symbols.name: edges
symbols.note: Dictionary mapping relation names to lists of edge dicts.

symbols.name: site_counts
symbols.note: Dictionary tracking site-level counts (total, annotated, missing, etc.).

symbols.name: cov
symbols.note: Coverage dictionary for parameters, returns, fields, bases, and functions.

symbols.name: counters
symbols.note: Dictionary counting outcomes (RESOLVED, UNRESOLVED, AMBIGUOUS, etc.).

symbols.name: structural_matches
symbols.note: Count of structural inheritance matches found.

symbols.name: overmatched
symbols.note: List of protocol nodes that exceeded STRUCTURAL_MAX_MATCHES.

symbols.name: fan_in
symbols.note: Dictionary mapping target node IDs to sets of reference strings for hub detection.

symbols.name: hubs
symbols.note: Sorted list of hub target IDs exceeding hub_cap.

symbols.name: hub_set
symbols.note: Set of hub target IDs for fast lookup.

symbols.name: suppressed
symbols.note: Count of edges suppressed by hub cap.

symbols.name: lang_report
symbols.note: Dictionary indicating language support (only Python supported).

symbols.name: coverage
symbols.note: Aggregated coverage dictionary with all counts, samples, and hub info.

claims.text: ``class C(Base, metaclass=M)`` -- parse.py keeps keyword arguments in ``bases`` as written. A metaclass is not a base and must not become an ``inherits`` edge.
claims.why: The code explicitly checks `if "=" in base.split("[", 1)[0]: continue`, which skips bases containing '=' (like metaclass=M). This matches the claim.

claims.text: An Enum member is a VALUE, not a typed field: parse.py forces its annotation to "" precisely so no member->type edge can be fabricated for it, and ``emit`` will count it as missing.
claims.why: The claim about parse.py forcing annotation to "" for Enum members cannot be verified because the chunk does not include parse.py. The code does emit a site with `raw=decl.annotation`, but we cannot check if that annotation is forced to "" for Enum members.

The code implements a heuristic: it collects member names via `_member_names`, computes `wanted` for protocols, and finds nodes with superset of those members. The comment accurately describes the approach.

claims.text: Told us nothing: the whole match set is dropped rather than truncated, because the first N of an arbitrary set is a guess.
claims.why: When `len(matches) > STRUCTURAL_MAX_MATCHES`, the code does not add any matches for that protocol (no `for node_id in matches` iteration). The match set is entirely dropped, as claimed.

claims.text: hub cap (I6): measured, applied, and published
claims.why: The code measures fan_in, identifies hubs, suppresses edges, and includes hub info in coverage. However, the variable `hub_cap` is not defined in this chunk; its value and the condition `if hub_cap` cannot be verified. The claim is partially checkable but depends on external definition.

claims.text: NEVER a numeric 0: the tree-sitter path has no class/field vocabulary, so "we did not look" must not read as "we looked and found none". Stufe 1 is Python only.
claims.why: For non-Python languages, the code sets `lang_report[lang] = "not_supported"` (a string), not a numeric 0. The comment correctly explains the rationale.

observations.what: The `emit` function updates `site_counts` but does not update `cov` counts; `cov` is updated separately in the loops that call `emit`. This is consistent with the structure.
The structural matching uses `_member_names` function which is not defined in this chunk; its behavior is uncheckable.
The hub capping logic relies on `hub_cap` and `_CAPPED_RELATIONS` which are not defined in this chunk; their values and correctness cannot be verified.
The `coverage` dictionary includes `edges_before_hub_cap` which is computed before hub capping, but the variable `raw_by_relation` is defined and used correctly.
